from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Two prisoners face a grid of sixty-four coins.", 
                         "One coin must be flipped to earn freedom.", 
                         "Can they coordinate a strategy for success?"]
        self.setup_layout("The Prisoner's Dilemma", lecture_lines)
        
        alice = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FF0000", fill_opacity=1)
        bob = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=1)
        link = DashedLine(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT, color="#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(alice, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(bob, 'B5')
        self.play(FadeIn(alice), FadeIn(bob))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        link.put_start_and_end_on(alice.get_center(), bob.get_center())
        self.play(Create(link))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.play(Indicate(alice), Indicate(bob))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Parity Principle", [
            "Parity tracks the state of a sequence.",
            "XOR operations determine if parity is even.",
            "Flipping one coin always reverses the parity."
        ])
        
        # Binary string: 1 0 1 1 0
        bits_str = "1 0 1 1 0"
        bits = VGroup(*[Text(c, font_size=36, color="#00FFFF") for c in bits_str.split()])
        bits.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(bits, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        bits_label = Text("Bits:", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        bits_label.next_to(bits, UP, buff=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), Write(bits), Write(bits_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        xor_text = Text("1 ⊕ 0 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 0 = 1", font_size=28, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(xor_text, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(xor_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # Highlight last bit and flip
        target_bit = bits[-1]
        self.play(Indicate(target_bit, color="#FF00FF"))
        
        new_bit = Text("1", font_size=36, color="#FF00FF")
        new_bit.move_to(target_bit)
        
        self.play(Transform(target_bit, new_bit))
        
        final_xor = Text("1 ⊕ 0 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 1 ⊕ 1 = 0", font_size=28, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(final_xor, "E3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(xor_text, final_xor))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping Information to Geometry", [
            "Label every grid square with binary coordinates.",
            "The XOR sum of heads marks a square.",
            "Flipping that coin forces the board's parity."
        ])
        
        # Grid visual components
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(7):
            grid_lines.add(Line(self.grid["A1"] + np.array([-0.4, 0.4, 0]), self.grid["F1"] + np.array([-0.4, -0.4, 0]) + [i*0.8, 0, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2))
            grid_lines.add(Line(self.grid["A1"] + np.array([-0.4, 0.4, 0]), self.grid["A6"] + np.array([0.4, 0.4, 0]) + [0, -i*0.8, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(Create(grid_lines))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        data_point = Circle(radius=0.2, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(data_point, 'C3')
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(data_point))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.play(Indicate(data_point, color=RED))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: Decoding the Secret", [
            "The second prisoner calculates the total XOR sum.",
            "The result reveals the specific coin changed.",
            "The prisoners' secret strategy guarantees their escape."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display title (already added) and change color of line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        path = VGroup()
        for i in range(1, 7):
            start = self.grid[f"A{i}"]
            end = self.grid[f"F{i}"]
            path.add(Line(start, end, color="#00FF00"))
        
        self.play(Create(path), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        # Represent result via intersections
        points = VGroup()
        for i in ["B2", "C4", "E5"]:
            dot = Dot(self.grid[i], color="#FF00FF")
            points.add(dot)
            
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # Final flourish
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(points, color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Information Density", [
            "This strategy uses basic Hamming code principles.",
            "We encode information into simple parity checks.",
            "The grid becomes an error-correcting storage device."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display title (already shown in setup)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FFFF") for _ in range(12)])
        grid_positions = [f"{r}{c}" for r in "ABCDEF" for c in "123456"]
        import random
        selected_positions = random.sample(grid_positions, 12)
        
        animations = []
        for i, dot in enumerate(dots):
            self.place_at_grid(dot, selected_positions[i], scale_factor=0.5)
            animations.append(FadeIn(dot))
        
        self.play(*animations)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # Group points together to show high density
        self.play(
            FadeOut(dots),
            *[FadeIn(Dot(color="#FF0000", radius=0.2).move_to(self.grid["C3"]).scale(0.5 + i*0.05)) for i in range(5)]
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Impossible Chessboard: Decoding Information Theory
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic interest in logic and computer science

sections.title: The Hook: The Prisoner's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the problem: A warden forces a prisoner to flip one coin on an 8x8 grid of 64 coins. A second prisoner must identify the specific coin flipped to earn freedom. Can they coordinate a strategy to guarantee success?
sections.example: Visualize a 64-square grid with random coins (Heads/Tails) and two agents: 'Alice the Observer' and 'Bob the Guesser'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Parity Principle
sections.content: Explain the concept of 'Parity'—the idea that a sequence of bits can hold a 'checksum'. Introduce the XOR operation (0+0=0, 1+1=0, 0+1=1).
sections.example: A row of 3 coins: (H, T, H). Assign H=1, T=0. Sum = 1+0+1 = 2. The parity is 'Even' (0). Changing one coin flips the parity.

sections.title: Mapping Information to Geometry
sections.content: Assign each square on the chessboard a unique coordinate index from 0 to 63 (represented in binary: 000000 to 111111). We aim to make the XOR sum of all 'Heads' positions equal to the index of the square to be flipped.
sections.example: If the sum of all 'Heads' squares is 010111 (binary for 23), then the prisoner flips the coin at square 23 to force the board parity to match the target secret.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Decoding the Secret
sections.content: Explain how the second prisoner calculates the XOR sum of all 'Heads' squares on the board. The result tells them exactly which square the first prisoner changed.
sections.example: Visual animation: The board shifts from a random state to one where the XOR sum points precisely to the 'changed' coordinate, acting like a pointer.

sections.title: Conclusion: Information Density
sections.content: Summarize that this is an application of Hamming Codes. We have encoded 6 bits of information (the coordinate) into 64 bits of state, proving that information can be 'compressed' into parity checks.
sections.example: An analogy: Like a QR code, the entire board functions as a single error-correcting storage device where the 'error' is actually the message itself.
